_doc: Real 3D models for the flight labs, loaded by vehicle-glb.js. Every entry is optional: when its file is missing the labs use their procedural model. See README.md and ../rockets/README.md. Per-entry extras: assemble (move exploded parts back), centerBand, maxMetalness / envMapIntensity (loader-side material repair), noFit (catalogue must not stretch to the catalogue height), note (shown after the credit line).

full.note: whole Falcon 9: first stage, interstage, second stage, fairing

tank.note: first-stage tank only; y = 0 is the bottom of the tank (engines hang below), the length is overridden per vehicle by the Shipyard

firstStage.note: booster with interstage: what lands. Real first stage 41.2 m + interstage ~5 m + grid-fin skirt

legs.note: the model has the four legs stowed along the base; the lab hides them and animates its own legs (stowed -> deployed, 18 m span)

gridFins.note: titanium grid fins, folded flat in the model; the lab hides them and draws its own steerable ones

legs.note: one merged mesh: legs cannot be separated or animated, so this is a static display model (never used for a landing)

2017-2019 BFR/Starship design with deployed landing legs, baked into the mesh. Real Starship (flights since 2023) has no legs and lands on the tower arms; this is a historical/HLS-style display model only. Original 30 MB / 343k triangles, web copy 0.23 MB / 51k triangles (decimated with --soup).

parts.name: Nose, header tank and forward flaps
Propellant tank section and aft flaps
Raptor engines, thrust structure and leg feet

saturn-v.title: Apollo | Saturn V Launch Vehicle
saturn-v.author: devPilot
saturn-v.note: launch vehicle only, up to the Instrument Unit (88.1 m modelled; the real stages plus IU are ~85.6 m). No Apollo CSM, spacecraft/LM adapter or launch escape tower, which make up the rest of the 110.6 m

full.note: S-IC, S-II, S-IVB and the Instrument Unit at 1:1; the author laid the interstage, the S-II/S-IVB skirt and the Instrument Unit out beside the stack with ~1 m gaps between the stages: `assemble` moves them back onto the stack and closes the gaps

space-shuttle-stack.title: GeoFS Official Space Shuttle Atlantis (OV-104)
space-shuttle-stack.author: AF267
space-shuttle-stack.note: Atlantis with its External Tank and SRBs (launch configuration)

full.note: full launch stack (orbiter, orange External Tank, two SRBs), not orbiter-only. Scaled so the whole stack is 56.1 m; the orbiter comes out ~12 % short of 37.2 m against the tank and boosters

sls-block-1.title: NASA SLS Block 1 Crew V4
sls-block-1.author: Clarence365
sls-block-1.note: Block 1 Crew with launch abort system; horizontal size squeezed 4 % (widthScale) because the original is ~3 % too wide in the core and ~8 % in the boosters

atlas-v.title: Atlas V
atlas-v.author: SunnyChen754
atlas-v.note: modelled as Atlas V 551 (5 solid boosters, 5.4 m fairing; the file itself is named AtlasV551)

new-glenn.title: New Glenn (Better Version)
new-glenn.author: Wolfpack278
new-glenn.note: stylised; booster and upper stage come as two objects and are stacked for the full vehicle; the Landing Lab shows the booster only

full.note: first stage + upper stage with fairing stacked (the author supplies them side by side)

firstStage.note: booster only: what lands (lab length 57 m)

legs.note: no legs in the model (the real New Glenn legs fold inside the aft skirt); the Landing Lab draws its own 4 legs

controlSurfaces.note: strakes and flaps are part of the single merged booster mesh and cannot be separated or animated: the Landing Lab skips its own for this model

n1.title: N1 Rocket
n1.author: Soviet Model Magic
n1.note: N1-L3 (Moon version) with launch escape tower: 30 NK-15 first-stage engines (24 outer + 6 inner), 17 m base; stage-by-stage details not verified

parts.name: Block G / D, L3 lunar complex and shroud

electron.title: Electron - Rocket Lab
electron.author: Stanley Creative
electron.note: black carbon-composite finish, lit by the viewer

tank.note: first stage only; y = 0 is its base, the Shipyard overrides the length and the diameter

super-heavy-b18.title: Booster 18 (B18)
super-heavy-b18.author: Wolfpack278
super-heavy-b18.note: Block 3 (V3) Super Heavy named Booster 18 by the author (the real B18 was scrapped after a November 2025 test; B19 flew first); real Block 3 is 72.3 m, shown at the lab length 71 m in the Landing Lab; grid fins baked in

legs.note: Super Heavy has no landing legs (caught by the tower arms)

controlSurfaces.note: single merged mesh: lattice grid fins are baked in, so the Landing Lab skips its own grid fins for this model

ares-i.title: Ares 1 (A)
ares-i.author: NASA
ares-i.note: Ares I-A rocket only (no Orion, abort tower or pad in the file), 9.73 m per unit, 94 m. The body measures about 5.9 m across in the file (real 5.5 m), not corrected. The four detached duplicate meshes outside the rotated root are hidden. Stage bands (63 m and 82 m) are approximate, not from drawings. The original is Draco-compressed (the web copy is not).

jupiter-c.title: Explorer Jupiter-C Rocket
jupiter-c.author: NASA
jupiter-c.note: Rocket only (no satellite or pad in the file). 1.2135 m per unit, 21.2 m; body 1.83 m across (real 1.78 m). The original is Draco-compressed (the web copy is not). Stage bands are approximate.

redstone.title: Mercury-Redstone Launch Vehicle
redstone.author: Stanley Creative
redstone.note: Mercury-Redstone stack: the file includes the Mercury capsule and the launch escape tower on the Redstone booster (not the NASA Redstone file). Booster 1.78 m across. Scaled 25.4 m, which is the file at 1:1 (no correction). Tank and engine detail is not checked.

atlas-lv-3b.title: Atlas LV-3B Mercury
atlas-lv-3b.author: Stanley Creative
atlas-lv-3b.note: Mercury-Atlas: sustainer with the XLR-105, two XLR-89 booster engines, Mercury capsule and launch escape tower (the file has all of them). Scaled to 29 m. The two booster pods are one merged node, so they move as one group in the exploded view (no sideways slide).

v-2.title: V-2 Rocket
v-2.author: person
v-2.note: Untextured grey model with its tail fins. The file is 13.7 m long, scaled to 14 m (+2 %); the 1.65 m body matches the catalogue. The two explode sections (tail and body) are approximate.

energia.title: Energia Rocket (untextured)
energia.author: Soviet Model Magic
energia.note: Energia core with four strap-on boosters and the engine nozzles only. No Buran orbiter and no Polyus payload are in the file (the core top is bare). Scaled to 58.8 m (file 57.9 units, +1.6 %); the core measures about 7.9 m across. Untextured.

epsilon.title: JAXA Epsilon rocket
epsilon.author: rocket0314
epsilon.note: Three-section stack with a nozzle at the base. The file is 4.8 units tall, scaled to 24.4 m (5.07 m per unit). The body measures about 3.1 m across at this scale (catalogue 2.6 m), not corrected. Explode bands are approximate.

pslv.title: PSLV C40
pslv.author: Neel3Dartist
pslv.note: PSLV-XL with its six strap-on boosters (separate islands, shown as boosters in the exploded view). The core and upper stages are one merged mesh, so the three core sections (20 m and 40 m) are cut at approximate heights, not from drawings. Scaled to 44 m; the core measures about 3.0 to 3.3 m across and the strap-on ring about 5.4 m. The launch-pad lattice in the file is hidden.

lvm3.title: GSLV Mk3
lvm3.author: Jainesh Pathak
lvm3.note: LVM3 (the renamed GSLV Mk III) with its two S200 solid boosters, shown as boosters in the exploded view. The core and fairing are one merged mesh, so the bands at 32 m and 40 m are approximate. Scaled to 43.5 m; the file core measured about 4.6 m across, squeezed 13 % (widthScale 0.87) to the catalogue 4 m.

long-march-5.title: Long March 5 rocket
long-march-5.author: andertan
long-march-5.note: Long March 5 with its four boosters (split from the merged booster mesh by corner, shown as boosters in the exploded view), core and fairing. Scaled to 56.97 m. The core measures about 5.4 m across (catalogue 5 m), not corrected. The core / fairing split at 40 m is approximate.

terran-1.title: Relativity Space Terran 1
terran-1.author: Clarence365
terran-1.note: Terran 1 (3D-printed; its only flight in 2023 did not reach orbit). The file body is 2.75 m across at 33.5 m, squeezed 18 % (widthScale 0.82) to the catalogue 2.25 m. The explode bands (base, body, nose) are approximate.

neutron.title: Rocketlab Neutron Rocket
neutron.author: Clarence365
neutron.note: Early design: the file is a 43 m stack whose body measures about 6.1 m across (catalogue 7 m, not stretched sideways). Nine engine bells, a cargo fairing on top. The proportions and engine layout are the author’s, not the final Neutron. Explode bands are approximate.

firefly-alpha.title: Firefly Alpha Rocket
firefly-alpha.author: rocket0314
firefly-alpha.note: Firefly Alpha: first stage with nine engine bells, second stage, fairing. Scaled to 29 m; 1.81 m across (catalogue 1.8 m). Explode bands (y) are approximate.

falcon-9-full-thrust.title: Falcon 9 - SpaceX
falcon-9-full-thrust.author: Stanley Creative
falcon-9-full-thrust.note: Falcon 9 Full Thrust (Stanley Creative). The file has its legs and fairing and is 59.3 m tall; scaled up to the catalogue 70 m (uniform, +18 %), which gives a body of about 3.6 m (real 3.66 m). The legs are deployed (out beyond the body, not stowed) and the grid fins are extended.

soyuz-fg.title: Soyuz-FG
soyuz-fg.author: Paculino
soyuz-fg.note: Soyuz-FG (no description in the source; 5k faces, low detail, accuracy not verified). APPROXIMATE STAND-IN for Soyuz-U (51.1 m), Soyuz-2.1a and Soyuz-2.1b (46.3 m each): the same Soyuz-FG model is used for those ids and is drawn at their catalogue heights (about 3 % longer for Soyuz-U, about 6 to 7 % shorter for Soyuz-2.1a and 2.1b), so it is not their exact geometry.

h-iia.title: H-IIA Rocket
h-iia.author: MarioK
h-iia.note: Stylised toy-like model (exaggerated features, simple colours), variant not stated by the author. Drawn at the H-IIA 202 height (53 m). APPROXIMATE STAND-IN for H-II (49 m) and H-IIB (56.6 m) as well: those ids use this model at their own heights (about 7 % shorter for H-II, about 7 % longer for H-IIB).

long-march-2f.title: LongMarch-2F Shenjian (converted from STL)
long-march-2f.author: 长江学者AmethystY98 (AmethystY98)
long-march-2f.note: Converted by us from the Wikimedia Commons STL (CC BY-SA 4.0, ShareAlike: this derived copy is under the same licence; the STL is simple and untextured, with flat normals). Scaled to 58.34 m. Single merged mesh, so the exploded view is approximate.

safir.title: Safir Satellite Launch Vehicle
safir.author: JamesMartinCNS
safir.note: Low detail (5k faces, no description). Accuracy against the real Safir is unverified (fin count, nozzle and fairing are the author's). Drawn at its catalogue length (22 m).

proton-m.title: Proton-K with Zarya ISS module (stand-in for Proton-M)
proton-m.author: Soviet Model Magic
proton-m.note: STAND-IN: this is the older Proton-K carrying the Zarya module, not the Proton-M (catalogue 58.2 m, 7.4 m). The Zarya payload is part of the file and is kept. Proportions and the booster layout are the author's, not checked against drawings.

ariane-5.title: Ariane 5
ariane-5.author: Yanis
ariane-5.note: The author says the model is not 100 % accurate. Decimated to about 82k triangles for the web. Drawn at the catalogue ECA height (50.5 m).

titan-iv.title: Titan IV
titan-iv.author: AllThingsSpace
titan-iv.note: Titan IV (IVB figures, 44 m). The file has an exploded-view arrangement of the vehicle beside the stack, and a second copy: the web copy is cropped to the assembled stack (all triangles on the far side of the stack are removed), and the specular-gloss material is converted to metal-rough. Accuracy of the parts is not checked.

sea-dragon.title: Sea Dragon Rocket
sea-dragon.author: IkaetieIke
sea-dragon.note: CONCEPT (1962 Truax design, never built): the model is the author's 150 m two-stage concept, decimated to about 250k triangles for the web. Its own escape tower, which the author marks as incomplete, is hidden.

vega-c.title: Vega-C
vega-c.author: SethAlevy
vega-c.note: Concept CAD inspired by Vega-C (the author says so), accuracy doubtful. Decimated with a topology-free simplifier to about 123k triangles, so some surfaces may be open. Drawn at 35 m.

starship-stack.title: Starship full stack (Super Heavy + Starship, merged by us)
starship-stack.author: Sharpraptor
starship-stack.note: CRUDE, LOW DETAIL. Two Sharpraptor models joined by us into one file (Super Heavy from https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/ee8644e6f8c94931b09d03b498be6fc6, Starship from https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/115c011815f347c8a30af2eaff4c9555; both CC BY 4.0): booster at the bottom (72.3 m, 9 m across), Starship on top with its base at the booster top (48.7 m, body 9 m, flaps about 22 m across). Neither part is checked against drawings; no hot-staging ring or interstage is modelled separately.

engines._doc: Standalone rocket-engine models, loaded by vehicle-glb.js (preloadEngineModel / engineModel). The file is oriented (axis/noseSign: nozzle exit at the -axis end when noseSign is omitted), the bell exit ring is measured from the geometry, and the clone is scaled so the exit is exitDiameterM wide. Placed on vehicles by shipyard.html and view3d.js, shown alone in spacecraft.html (labs.catalog). Original author credit is required (CC BY 4.0).

generic-engine.title: Rocket Engine
generic-engine.author: ~Drift~ (QuickDriftVR)
generic-engine.use: generic bell engine (library / catalogue only: not placed on a vehicle)
